entry.title: PhotoCraft: Open-Source Photoshop Reimplementation in Rust
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | github.com | discussion | hacker news

The application is a clean-room reimplementation of Adobe Photoshop written entirely in Rust. It features support for layers, masks, adjustment layers, layer styles, typography, vectors, brushes, and real PSD files. To ensure high performance, it utilizes a GPU compositor on wgpu, copy-on-write tiles, and multithreaded filters, avoiding the use of Electron or web views.

Currently in early alpha, the software is available for macOS, Windows, Linux, FreeBSD, and via WebAssembly. The engine is designed to be "agent-ready," allowing control through a command-line interface, a JSON control channel, or an MCP server. It is intended as an offline, non-subscription-based alternative for professional image editing workflows.

entry.title: Technical Analysis of the Skyrim Magelight XP Glitch
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | blog.alexbeals.com | discussion

A glitch in The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim allows players to gain massive Alteration experience by casting the Magelight spell near specific terrain, such as the mountains outside Solitude. The projectile's interaction with the L_TRANSPARENT_SMALL collision layer causes the error; because this layer is exempt from the "HandleHit" function that normally stops projectiles, the spell triggers a collision event on every frame until it has passed halfway through the object.

Analysis using TES5Edit and Cheat Engine confirms the glitch is caused by collision layer mechanics rather than travel distance or weather effects. The investigation identifies the specific interaction between the LightSpellProjectile and the game's collision detection logic that enables the unintended, continuous XP gain.

entry.title: Reverse Engineering NovaLogic's Comanche Terrain Maps
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | pikuma.com | discussion

The terrain map files for the 1992 game Comanche: Maximum Overkill consist of 1024×1024 heightmaps and color maps used for Voxel Space rendering. These assets are stored in .DTA files that must be decoded to reconstruct the landscape data.

The files are modified PCX images featuring a 128-byte custom header and run-length encoding (RLE) compression. The technical process involves writing an ANSI C program to decode the pixel data and hidden 256-color palettes into standard BMP images.

entry.title: ldraw-nova Uses AI Agents to Generate LEGO Models
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | github.com | hacker news

AI agents in ldraw-nova generate buildable LEGO models in the LDraw assembly language by producing Python-based generator scripts. This approach circumvents the spatial reasoning limitations typical of LLMs, resulting in LDraw source code, 3D/VR-ready views, and Blender-compatible .glb files.

Optimized for high-end models like Claude Opus 5.5 and Astra, the tool includes features for collision detection, headless rendering, and semantic part searching via jev-rerank. It supports immersive VR viewing on Meta Quest 3 and is deployed using Docker.

entry.title: PasRISCV RISC-V Emulator Enables In-Game Linux for SEEDS
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | againstallodds.games | discussion | hacker news

PasRISCV is an open-source RISC-V 64-bit emulator written in Object Pascal that provides a fully emulated Alpine Linux system for the game SEEDS. The system simulates a complete virtual machine—including CPU, memory, and I/O—allowing native Linux binaries to run on a host machine.

The emulator features a hybrid CPU model using an interpreter and a tracing JIT compiler for x86-64 hosts and supports RVA23 and SMP. Integration is handled via Linux Virtual Sockets (vsock) to facilitate high-speed communication between the game engine and the guest system.
